edges.description: Reduced removal of cell-surface terminal lysines could increase plasminogen binding. This is an extrapolation from purified-enzyme experiments to patient deficiency.
Functional deficiency is detectable by a plasma enzyme assay.
Prolonged B2-receptor signaling is a plausible contributor to vascular leakage. Carboxypeptidase-deficient mice support this link, but the study did not measure bradykinin levels.
Histamine-mediated vascular effects are a plausible component of the phenotype; their contribution in individual patients is uncertain.
Vascular fluid leakage produces episodic subcutaneous and submucosal swelling.
Superficial vascular leakage contributes to wheals, which can accompany angioedema but are not obligatory.
Intestinal angioedema can produce painful abdominal attacks.
Upper-airway fluid extravasation can produce laryngeal swelling.

Greater cell-surface plasminogen binding could facilitate plasmin activation and downstream kallikrein-kinin activation. The proposed intermediates have not been directly quantified in CPN-deficient patients.
Additional kinin production could increase ligand availability on a background of impaired catabolism.
Drug inhibition can further impair peptide disposal in a patient with reduced activity of several catabolic enzymes. The contribution attributable to CPN alone is unresolved.
edges.source: Angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor and dipeptidyl-peptidase-4 inhibitor exposure

edges.description: Adding active enzyme decreases binding, the inverse of the proposed effect of deficiency.
edges.limitations: Neither patient-derived cells nor a CPN1-deficient cellular genotype was studied. Enhanced binding and kinin generation in patients were not measured. CPN did not reduce tPA-induced whole-blood clot lysis in the parallel assay.

edges.description: Complete loss of the enzyme, with the resulting anaphylatoxin persistence read out as lethal sensitivity to complement activation.
edges.limitations: The mouse has complete enzyme loss, whereas measured human deficiency is partial. It demonstrates susceptibility to acute experimental complement activation rather than the spontaneous recurrent attacks of the human illness.

edges.description: Antihistamine pretreatment reduced mortality following C5a challenge, supporting a histamine-mediated contribution.
edges.limitations: Antihistamine rescue supports a histamine-dependent component of acute mouse lethality; it does not establish histamine as the sole or necessary mediator of every spontaneous human attack.

edges.description: Challenge-induced leakage supports a role for CPN in vascular barrier protection.
edges.limitations: Bradykinin was not measured, so substrate attribution was inferred. The model uses experimental skin irritation rather than spontaneous human attacks.

nodes.description: ACE inhibitors and DPP-4 inhibitors can worsen angioedema when parallel peptide-degrading pathways are impaired. A 2014 patient with reduced ACE, aminopeptidase P and CPN activity improved after lisinopril withdrawal and became attack-free after sitagliptin withdrawal. This related biochemical case did not establish an inherited CPN1 genotype and does not show that all CPN deficiency requires drug exposure.

The response does not establish drug exposure as necessary for hereditary CPN1 disease.
